environment.contention_note: How busy the machine was. This belongs next to the driver version and the CPU model for the same reason those do: it changes the answer. The same device, build and test measured 9.5x apart on host command-buffer recording depending only on what else was running (docs/PERF.md §10). metric_of_record.islands_equal_claimed_nodes_note: two independent counters. Per R9 (DESIGN.md §10.0.1) agreement raises confidence, not evidence; the falsifier is `dispatch_accounting`, which goes red if the islands did not all run.
metric_of_record.largest_island_flops_note: the EP now *emits* the key on its `vulkan.getcapability` trace event, but emits 0: `CoverageReport` computes no FLOP estimate, and `PartitionStats.island_count` is 0 on the same event while `subgraphs_live` is not. The slot is plumbed and unfilled. It is reported as null here rather than as 0, because 'not computed' and 'zero FLOPs' are different states and only one of them is a measurement.
metric_of_record.quiescence_note: a second gate, alongside model_output_equivalence. The same device, build and test measured 9.5x apart on host recording time depending only on what else was running on the machine, so a timing taken on a contended box is not a slower measurement of the same thing — it is a measurement of a different machine.

analysis.time_in_compute_note: the sum of vulkan.subgraph spans — the EP's own view of time inside Compute. It is NOT the process wall clock: ORT's own graph execution, the CPU EP's nodes between islands, and session setup are all outside it. Phase shares below are shares of this, and may not be restated as shares of the benchmark's wall time.

record.caveat: NOT A LEAF: this span also contains desc_alloc, pipeline_lookup, cmd_upload. Its total is an upper bound on record itself, not a measurement of it. Quoting it as 'record' attributes a child's cost to the parent's name.

analysis.nested_phases_note: sub-record spans, reported separately because they are INSIDE vulkan.record. They are excluded from host_phases_ms and from every share, since adding them to their own parent counts the same microseconds twice.

phase_nesting.asserts: the phases summed as siblings do not overlap, so the host total counts each microsecond once
phase_nesting.detail: containment and caveats agree; nested = cmd_upload, desc_alloc, pipeline_lookup

decomposition_identity.asserts: a published decomposition closes against a whole measured by a different instrument than the parts

internal_closure.why_weak: both sides are sums over the same tracer's spans. A cost hidden inside a row cancels from both and this check stays green — which is precisely how '68.3+16.3+14.1+0.3 = 99.0%' closed while missing a 2 GB memcpy. Never quote this as evidence that the rows are correctly named.

external_closure.whole_source: the traced worker's own perf_counter around the warmup+timed run loop

decomposition_identity.detail: the trace accounts for 5579.7 ms inside Compute but the harness's own clock measured only 5121.2 ms of wall time for the same work (1.09x). Time is being counted more than once. Two independent clocks disagreeing is not a rounding question.

phase_leaf_accounting.asserts: a phase total is only quoted under its own name when that span contains no other accounted work
phase_leaf_accounting.detail: record: 69.1% of it is desc_alloc+pipeline_lookup+cmd_upload, leaf residual 892.3 ms

analysis.unattributed_note: time inside vulkan.subgraph that no phase span covers: reading ORT input pointers, buffer allocation and descriptor-pool work before recording, the readback memcpy and the writes into ORT's output tensors after the fence. It is reported rather than folded into a neighbouring phase, because a phase split whose parts do not sum to the whole should say so.

anchor_quality.detail: device-lane spans may sit up to 119.2 ms from their true host position. Durations are unaffected; positions are not evidence. Attribution is ordinal for exactly this reason.

analysis.gpu_note: summed from the per-span gpu_ns float, not from the integer-microsecond `dur`: several of these kernels run in 2-3 us, where truncation is a 15-30% error over thousands of spans.

record_scaling.composition_note: vulkan.record is not one activity. It brackets vkBeginCommandBuffer through vkEndCommandBuffer, and the host memcpy of this island's inputs into staging buffers happens inside it. The two are reported separately because they have different fixes: the memcpy goes away if the data stops being re-copied per Compute call; the residual is the recording loop itself.
record_scaling.size_detail: every island in this run has the same dispatch count, so island size does not vary and this run cannot say whether recording scales with it. Not a refutation.
record_scaling.warmup_shape_note: cycles_to_steady is the first inference whose mean record cost is within 25% of the median of the last three. A value of 2 means the cost is a one-off paid on inference 1 and everything after it is steady state — a fixed cost to amortise, not a curve to fit.
record_scaling.decline_detail: the decline holds within island identity: 100% of islands record faster on their last inference than on their first, and the per-cycle means fall across cycles that each contain exactly the same 1 islands in the same order. It is a warmup effect, not an island-mix artifact. Shape: RAMP_OVER_3_INFERENCES (steady within 25% of the tail median 22.132 ms from inference 3). It has NOT flattened: the last three cycle means still span 1.587×, so the steady state is not established and the steady-state median is provisional.

gpu_steady_tail.detail: a suffix of 5 inference(s) holds within 1.2959% RSD, but it is 12% of the 43 usable inferences and 38 were discarded to find it. Floors: n >= 8 and coverage >= 50%. The RSD bar constrains the tail's internal spread, not its agreement with the device's true steady rate, so a short flat suffix passes it just as well as a settled one. No GPU figure is quotable from this run; the suffix's median is kept under `withheld_median_ms` so it cannot be read as one.

steady_state.gpu_busy_note: GPU busy overlaps submit+fence_wait and is NOT a sibling of the host phases — it is printed as a share of the same denominator so the two can be compared, never so they can be added. `fence_wait_gpu_idle` is the part of the fence wait the GPU was demonstrably not executing in, and it is the only GPU-idle figure that may be quoted.
steady_state.duration_caveat: these are durations and durations move with machine load. The *structure* here — that recording is paid on every inference rather than once, and that the cold inference is a different workload from the warm ones — is a count of spans and survives contention. The percentages do not.
steady_state.gpu_steady_tail_reanalysed: re-derived from the preserved trace after the 2026-08-01 coverage floor landed (phases.GPU_TAIL_QUOTABLE_MIN_N/GPU_TAIL_MIN_COVERAGE). The verdict this file was written with was STEADY / median 37.562 ms; it is superseded, not deleted, so the change is visible to a reader of the artifact.
